blocks.text: Claude 的这两项结果都依赖全息对偶，即某些包含引力的宇宙可以用一个完全不含引力的量子理论精确描述。在第一个问题中，物理学家在 1983 年已经证明，随着这类宇宙升温，黑洞会像水沸腾一样突然形成；但他们的方法只适用于大到足以让相对论成立的大宇宙。2003 年有人提出了一个计算方案，用来判断在只能使用量子描述的极小宇宙中是否同样如此，但计算量太大，无法完成。Fable 5.2 基本自主地完成了这项计算，发现那里的转变同样是突变的。在第二个问题中，物理学家 15 年多来一直用一种技术在简化宇宙中排除量子引力的候选理论，Fable 5.2 找到了该技术的精确极限。关于这些结果的更多内容，请参阅各自的预印本：这里和这里。

blocks.text: 蛋白质折叠

腺相关病毒是一种小型无害病毒，其蛋白质外壳（即衣壳）可用于递送基因疗法。衣壳的蛋白质结构很重要——例如，它会影响疗法是否会被患者的免疫系统阻断——但同时也极其复杂。现有的蛋白质折叠模型（如 AlphaFold）能预测单个蛋白质，而一个衣壳却由数十个蛋白质组装而成。Claude Mythos 5.2 在两个开源蛋白质折叠模型的基础上，找到了一种准确预测整个衣壳结构的新方法。它编写代码，让这些模型在相互重叠的蛋白质链分组上运行，再利用已知的衣壳对称性信息将它们合并起来。

blocks.text: 如何构建能在模型部署前可靠捕捉每一次失败的评估，这个问题仍未解决。评估能力极强的模型往往情况复杂，难以看清全貌——例如，Claude Mythos 5.2 和 Fable 5.2 都比我们近期的任何模型更频繁地表达出怀疑自己正在被评估，这给我们判断它们在真实环境中会如何行动带来了挑战。随着未来模型的应用场景不断扩大、能力不断增强，我们预计这一挑战还会加剧。正因如此，我们不会仅靠这些评估来全面了解安全状况：我们还会借助训练期间的监控、对内部使用记录的审查、外部评估者的测试，以及用于检查模型内部情况的可解释性技术。我们也在努力让评估更贴近现实，并更好地理解评估遗漏了什么。

blocks.text: 安全保障

网络安全与生物学保障。与之前的 Claude Fable 模型一致，Fable 5.2 配备了安全分类器，可拦截高风险的网络活动，包括渗透测试、漏洞利用生成和基于二进制的漏洞，以及研究生物学中的大多数任务。当查询被拦截时，用户会改为收到来自 Opus 4.8（网络安全）和 Opus 5（生物学）的回复。自 Claude Fable 5.1 发布以来，我们持续降低安全分类器的误报率。基于在 claude.ai、Claude Code 和 Cowork 上的早期测试，我们发现 Fable 5.2 的拦截次数比 Fable 5.1 减少了约 55%——网络安全领域减少约 60%，生物学领域减少约 40%。Claude Mythos 5.2 面向在这些两用领域开展工作的经过审核的组织开放。

blocks.text: AI 研发。Claude Fable 5.2 和 Claude Mythos 5.2 背后的模型在通用能力上又前进了一步。不过在训练过程中，我们采取措施，限制了那些最可能直接加速 AI 研发的特定研究能力。因此在加速器内核优化、改进大语言模型架构等相关领域，Fable 5.2 和 Claude Mythos 5.2 的表现大约相当于 Opus 5.5。需要强调的是，我们确保这些训练调整没有影响相关能力，比如智能体编程、硬件开发，以及传统的 AI 或机器学习研究（包括可解释性研究）。模型向用户提供服务时（也就是推理阶段），我们不会改动这些能力。正如系统卡第 1.5 节所述，与之前的模型类似，Fable 5.2 和 Claude Mythos 5.2 在该领域的少数话题上也会透明地回退到 Opus 5，其中包括某些非标准加速器上的内核开发。

blocks.text: Safety and alignment. To help ensure safety and alignment keep step with growing model capabilities, we ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes. We believe high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1’s but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks.

blocks.text: When to use Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Fable and Mythos are best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work. For most coding and knowledge tasks, we recommend that users start with Claude Opus 5.5, our strongest daily driver, and then switch to a different model as required, depending on the scope and complexity of their work—upward to Fable or Mythos, or downward to Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5. Fable 5.2 can also play the role of Advisor (where Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus models consult it to help solve harder problems) or Orchestrator (where it delegates simpler tasks to smaller models).

Important tasks in science, engineering, and mathematics increasingly depend on coding: analyzing data, modeling molecules, designing parts, and controlling instruments are all done through software. Below, we discuss how Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 have helped researchers make progress on difficult problems in these areas.

blocks.text: Theoretical physics
Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes, and the effort to unite the two linchpin theories of modern physics, relativity, and quantum mechanics.

inlines.text: Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes, and the effort to unite the two linchpin theories of modern physics, relativity, and quantum mechanics.

blocks.text: Both of Claude’s results rely on holographic duality, the idea that certain universes containing gravity can be precisely described by a quantum theory containing no gravity at all. In the first problem, physicists in 1983 had shown that as these universes heat up, black holes form abruptly, like water boiling; but their method worked only in large universes that were big enough for relativity to apply. A calculation to determine whether the same was true in very small universes, where only the quantum description can be used, was laid out in 2003 but was too laborious to complete. Fable 5.2, working largely autonomously, completed it and found the transition is abrupt there, too. In the second problem, Fable 5.2 found the exact limit of a technique physicists have used for more than 15 years to rule out candidate theories of quantum gravity in a simplified universe. Read more about these results in their respective preprints, here and here.

blocks.text: Protein folding

Adeno-associated viruses are small, harmless viruses whose protein shell, the capsid, can be used to deliver gene therapies. The protein structure of the capsid is important—for example, it affects whether the therapy will be blocked by a patient’s immune system—but it’s also highly complex. Existing protein-folding models like AlphaFold can predict individual proteins, but a capsid is built from dozens of them. Building on two open-source protein-folding models, Claude Mythos 5.2 found a novel way to accurately predict a whole capsid’s structure. It wrote code that ran these models on overlapping groups of protein chains, and used the information on the known symmetries of the capsid to merge them together.

blocks.text: Mathematics

Mathematical formalization. Formalization is the process of translating a mathematical proof into a language that a computer can check step by step. It can help human mathematicians gain confidence in results without having to check them by hand (this matters even more when AI models generate results that are hard for humans to verify). Because formalization is such a laborious process, if AI could assist with it, mathematicians could spend more time exploring novel ideas.

blocks.text: Safety and alignment

No single test can tell us how a highly capable model will behave once it’s deployed, so we rely on many different tests and many different types of evidence before release. For the model underlying Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our predeployment safety work included alignment training and testing, newly designed evaluations on the model’s propensity to take unhelpful actions, building stronger safeguards against misuse, and scaling up our behavioral monitoring. The model was also tested before release by external evaluators, including the UK AI Security Institute, Frontier Design, and METR. See the Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 System Card for a summary of their reports⁴ and for a full description of our own safety and capabilities testing.

blocks.text: The problem of building evaluations that reliably catch every failure before a model is deployed remains unsolved. The complexities of evaluating highly capable models often muddy the picture—for example, Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. As these settings expand and capabilities increase with future models, we expect this challenge to grow. That is why we do not rely on these evaluations alone to provide a holistic picture of safety: we draw on monitoring during training, reviews of transcripts from internal use, testing by external evaluators, and interpretability techniques for examining what is happening inside the model. We are also working to make our evaluations more realistic and to better understand what they miss.

blocks.text: Safeguards

Cybersecurity and biology safeguards. Consistent with previous Claude Fable models, Fable 5.2 comes with safety classifiers that block high-risk cyber activities including penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability, as well as most tasks in research biology. Where a query is blocked, users will instead receive a response from Opus 4.8 for cybersecurity and Opus 5 for biology. Since the release of Claude Fable 5.1, we have continued to reduce false positives for our safety classifiers. Based on early testing across claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork, we observed about 55% fewer blocks with Fable 5.2 compared with Fable 5.1—about 60% fewer in cybersecurity and 40% fewer in biology. Claude Mythos 5.2 is available to vetted organizations that work in these dual use areas.

blocks.text: AI research and development. The model that underlies Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 is a step forward in general capabilities. However, during the model’s training, we took steps to limit advances in the specific research capabilities that could most directly accelerate AI development. Thus, in relevant areas, including accelerator kernel optimization and improving large language model architectures, Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 perform at about the level of Opus 5.5. Importantly, we ensured that the training changes did not affect related capabilities like agentic coding, hardware development, and traditional AI or machine learning research (including interpretability research). We do not alter these capabilities as the model is being served to users (that is, at inference time). As described in Section 1.5 of the system card and similarly to previous models, Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 also include transparent fallbacks to Opus 5 for a small set of topics in this domain, including kernel development on certain nonstandard accelerators.

blocks.text: Anti-distillation. Distillation, where a model is trained on the outputs of a more advanced one to extract the advanced model’s capabilities, occurs illicitly on an industrial scale, often involving thousands of fake Claude accounts. Since distillation allows for advanced capabilities to be released without the safeguards we’ve built into Claude, it creates safety and national security risks (see our September 2026 threat intelligence report for details on illicit distillation activity we’ve detected and disrupted so far). Fable 5.2 has the strongest protections against distillation of any model we’ve released; it uses the techniques we described in a recent report, which have reduced the data harvested by distillers by 90% to 99%.

inlines.text: Data privacy and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards

blocks.text: Some more complex forms of AI model misuse can be detected only when observing patterns across multiple requests. For this reason, powerful models like Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 rely on safeguards that monitor a window of usage data (as opposed to individual responses). With Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, automated safety monitoring is run on prompts and responses that are stored in a customer’s infrastructure, making it compatible with zero data retention (ZDR). Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in private beta with customers like Bridgewater, Salesforce, and Stripe.
